sentences.text: Author: Dipankar Datta Bench: Dipankar Datta  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL
APPEAL NO. OF 2025  [Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 18030 OF 2024]
SRIKANTH APPELLANT  VERSUS  THE STATE OF KARNATAKA RESPONDENT  ORDER 1.
Leave granted.
2. The appellant was driving a bus, which was involved in a fatal road accident.
The bus dashed one-Sanki Poojari @ Sanki Kotian (the deceased), who was walking on the left side of the road.
Being 75 years old, she succumbed to the injuries suffered in such accident.
3. There are concurrent findings of three courts convicting the appellant under Sections 279 and 304-A, Indian Penal Code, 18601.

The appellant has been sentenced to six months simple imprisonment together with fine of Rs.1,000/- each for the offences under Sections 279 and 304-A,
IPC.

4. We have heard Mr. C.B. Gururaj, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Mr. D.L.
Chidananda, learned counsel IPC appearing for the respondent-State of Karnataka.
5. The conviction under Section 304-A, IPC does not suffer from any infirmity and hence is affirmed.
However, the conviction under Section 279, IPC is set aside.

6. It appears from the documents placed on record that the jurisdictional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal2 on an approach being made by the family members of the deceased under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, awarded to them a sum of Rs.3,68,800/- (Rupees three lakh sixty-eight thousand eight hundred) only, with interest @ 6% p.a., towards just and fair compensation.

sentences.text: We are of the considered opinion that interest of justice would be best served if the offence under Section 304-A, IPC is compounded and the sentence of imprisonment, upon being set aside, is altered to increase in the fine, as ordered by the trial court, to Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakh), to be paid to the heirs of the deceased by the appellant.
Ordered accordingly.

8. Within a period of three months from date, the appellant shall deposit a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-
(Rupees two lakh) only with the relevant Claims Tribunal towards fine.
Thereafter, the Claims Tribunal shall ensure that such sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakh) only is distributed amongst the heirs of the deceased in equal shares.
Claims Tribunal 9.
Should such deposit be made, the sentence of imprisonment shall stand set aside and the appellant shall stand discharged of his bail bond.

However, in the event, no such deposit is made,
the appellant shall surrender before the trial court to serve the remainder of the term.
However, for a period of three months or till date the increased fine amount is deposited, whichever is earlier, the benefit of exemption from surrendering shall continue.
10. Immediately after expiry of three months from date, the relevant Claims Tribunal may intimate the Registry of this Court regarding compliance of the terms of this order.
If the appellant fails to comply, office shall seek directions.
11. The appeal stands disposed of on the above terms.
12. Pending application(s), if any, stand closed.
